about: Wrong answers that point to a specific misunderstanding about statistics and probability. 'pointsTo' is the subskill to work on. Claude's draft (2026-11-21), waiting for owner review.

misconceptions.description: Adds the data but forgets to divide by how many there are (or, for a missing value, doesn't take the others away).
Divides by the wrong number of values.
Gives the mean itself as the missing value.
Takes the middle of the list as written, without putting it in order first.
With an even number of values, picks one of the two middle numbers instead of averaging them.
Finds the mean when the question asks for the median.
Gives how many times the mode appears instead of the value itself.
Gives the middle value instead of the most common one.
Subtracts the first value listed from the last instead of smallest from largest.
Gives the largest value as the range.
Loses the negative when finding a range with negatives: 15 − (−4) done as 15 − 4.
Counts the columns of a dot plot instead of the dots.
Takes the middle of the number line as the median, instead of the middle dot.
Reads one bar when the question needs a difference or a total.
Adds the bars when the question asks how many more.
Reads a box edge (a quartile) as the median, or as the answer for the IQR.
Takes the median as halfway between the minimum and maximum.
Mixes up the range (max − min) and the interquartile range (Q3 − Q1).
Compares the favorable outcomes to the unfavorable ones (3 red to 5 others: 3/5) instead of to all outcomes (3/8).
Leaves some outcomes out of the total.
Gives the probability of the event when the question asks for NOT the event.
Multiplies the probabilities for "red or blue" from one pick (they add).
Adds the probabilities of two separate events happening together (they multiply).
Counts the times the event wouldn't happen.
